audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel / Shemuel Bet chapter 3, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for prolonged civil war, David's sons and plural marriages, Rizpah accusation, Abner's defection, Michal's forced transfer and Paltiel's grief, tribal negotiations, Joab's extrajudicial killing of Abner, David's disease/disability curse, public mourning, and political disavowal.

verses.restored: War was long between house of Saul and house of David. David grew stronger and stronger, while house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

familiar.text: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.

modern.text: Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

original.text: וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק וּבֵ֥ית שָׁא֖וּל הֹלְכִ֥ים וְדַלִּֽים

verses.restored: Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite.

familiar.text: And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;

modern.text: And sons were born to David in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;

original.text: וילדו לְדָוִ֛ד בָּנִ֖ים בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וַיְהִ֤י בְכוֹרוֹ֙ אַמְנ֔וֹן לַאֲחִינֹ֖עַם הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִֽת

verses.restored: His second was Chileab, by Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite; the third was Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.

familiar.text: And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

modern.text: his second was Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;

original.text: וּמִשְׁנֵ֣הוּ כִלְאָ֔ב לאביגל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֣ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִ֑י וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בֶּֽן מַעֲכָ֔ה בַּת תַּלְמַ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ גְּשֽׁוּר

verses.restored: The fourth was Adonijah son of Haggith; the fifth was Shephatiah son of Abital.

familiar.text: And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;

modern.text: his fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith; his fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital;

original.text: וְהָרְבִיעִ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּ֣ה בֶן חַגִּ֑ית וְהַחֲמִישִׁ֖י שְׁפַטְיָ֥ה בֶן אֲבִיטָֽל

verses.restored: The sixth was Ithream, by Eglah wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.

familiar.text: And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

modern.text: and his sixth was Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah. These sons were born to David in Hebron. Abner Joins David

original.text: וְהַשִּׁשִּׁ֣י יִתְרְעָ֔ם לְעֶגְלָ֖ה אֵ֣שֶׁת דָּוִ֑ד אֵ֛לֶּה יֻלְּד֥וּ לְדָוִ֖ד בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: While war continued between house of Saul and house of David, Abner was making himself strong in house of Saul.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.

modern.text: During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had continued to strengthen his position in the house of Saul.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְיוֹת֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וְאַבְנֵ֛ר הָיָ֥ה מִתְחַזֵּ֖ק בְּבֵ֥ית שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: Saul had a concubine, and her name was Rizpah daughter of Aiah. Ish-bosheth said to Abner, Why did you go in to my father's concubine?

familiar.text: And Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ishbosheth said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father’s concubine?

modern.text: Meanwhile, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. So Ish-bosheth questioned Abner, “Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?”

original.text: וּלְשָׁא֣וּל פִּלֶ֔גֶשׁ וּשְׁמָ֖הּ רִצְפָּ֣ה בַת אַיָּ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל אַבְנֵ֔ר מַדּ֥וּעַ בָּ֖אתָה אֶל פִּילֶ֥גֶשׁ אָבִֽי

verses.restored: Abner became very angry over words of Ish-bosheth and said, Am I a dog's head belonging to Judah? This day I do covenant-kindness with house of Saul your father, with his brothers and companions, and have not delivered you into hand of David; yet today you charge me with guilt concerning this woman.

familiar.text: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ishbosheth, and said, Am I a dog’s head, which against Judah do shew kindness this day unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David, that thou chargest me to day with a fault concerning this woman?

modern.text: Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation. “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?” he asked. “All this time I have been loyal to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not delivered you into the hand of David, but now you accuse me of wrongdoing with this woman!

original.text: וַיִּחַר֩ לְאַבְנֵ֨ר מְאֹ֜ד עַל דִּבְרֵ֣י אִֽישׁ בֹּ֗שֶׁת וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲרֹ֨אשׁ כֶּ֥לֶב אָנֹ֘כִי֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָה֒ הַיּ֨וֹם אֶֽעֱשֶׂה חֶ֜סֶד עִם בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֗יךָ אֶל אֶחָיו֙ וְאֶל מֵ֣רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְלֹ֥א הִמְצִיתִ֖ךָ בְּיַד דָּוִ֑ד וַתִּפְקֹ֥ד עָלַ֛י עֲוֺ֥ן הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַיּֽוֹם

verses.restored: Thus may Divine do to Abner, and thus add, if, as YHWH swore to David, I do not do so for him:

familiar.text: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the LORD hath sworn to David, even so I do to him;

modern.text: May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him:

original.text: כֹּֽה יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְאַבְנֵ֔ר וְכֹ֖ה יֹסִ֣יף ל֑וֹ כִּ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֔ד כִּֽי כֵ֖ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה לּֽוֹ

verses.restored: to transfer kingdom from house of Saul and establish throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.

familiar.text: To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.

modern.text: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”

original.text: לְהַֽעֲבִ֥יר הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה מִבֵּ֣ית שָׁא֑וּל וּלְהָקִ֞ים אֶת כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֗ד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְעַל יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע

verses.restored: Ish-bosheth could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.

familiar.text: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.

modern.text: And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.

original.text: וְלֹֽא יָכֹ֣ל ע֔וֹד לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת אַבְנֵ֖ר דָּבָ֑ר מִיִּרְאָת֖וֹ אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Abner sent messengers to David in his place, saying, Whose is land? Saying also, Make your covenant with me, and look, my hand will be with you to turn all Israel toward you.

familiar.text: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying also, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand shall be with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.

modern.text: Then Abner sent messengers in his place to say to David, “To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אַבְנֵ֨ר מַלְאָכִ֧ים אֶל דָּוִ֛ד תחתו לֵאמֹ֖ר לְמִי אָ֑רֶץ לֵאמֹ֗ר כָּרְתָ֤ה בְרִֽיתְךָ֙ אִתִּ֔י וְהִנֵּה֙ יָדִ֣י עִמָּ֔ךְ לְהָסֵ֥ב אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: David said, Good, I will make covenant with you. One thing I ask from you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.

familiar.text: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal Saul’s daughter, when thou comest to see my face.

modern.text: “Good,” replied David, “I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I require of you: Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ט֔וֹב אֲנִ֕י אֶכְרֹ֥ת אִתְּךָ֖ בְּרִ֑ית אַ֣ךְ דָּבָ֣ר אֶחָ֡ד אָנֹכִי֩ שֹׁאֵ֨ל מֵאִתְּךָ֤ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹא תִרְאֶ֣ה אֶת פָּנַ֔י כִּ֣י אִם לִפְנֵ֣י הֱבִיאֲךָ֗ אֵ֚ת מִיכַ֣ל בַּת שָׁא֔וּל בְּבֹאֲךָ֖ לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת פָּנָֽי

verses.restored: David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying, Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for one hundred foreskins of Philistines.

familiar.text: And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth Saul’s son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, which I espoused to me for an hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

modern.text: Then David sent messengers to say to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, “Give me back my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל אִֽישׁ בֹּ֥שֶׁת בֶּן שָׁא֖וּל לֵאמֹ֑ר תְּנָ֤ה אֶת אִשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת מִיכַ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ אֵרַ֣שְׂתִּי לִ֔י בְּמֵאָ֖ה עָרְל֥וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.

familiar.text: And Ishbosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel the son of Laish.

modern.text: So Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אִ֣ישׁ בֹּ֔שֶׁת וַיִּקָּחֶ֖הָ מֵ֣עִֽם אִ֑ישׁ מֵעִ֖ם פַּלְטִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן לוש

verses.restored: Her husband walked with her, going and weeping after her as far as Bahurim. Abner said to him, Go, return. And he returned.

familiar.text: And her husband went with her along weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return. And he returned.

modern.text: Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go back.” So he returned home.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אִתָּ֜הּ אִישָׁ֗הּ הָל֧וֹךְ וּבָכֹ֛ה אַחֲרֶ֖יהָ עַד בַּֽחֻרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו אַבְנֵ֛ר לֵ֥ךְ שׁ֖וּב וַיָּשֹֽׁב

verses.restored: Abner had spoken with elders of Israel, saying, In times past you were seeking David as king over you.

familiar.text: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, Ye sought for David in times past to be king over you:

modern.text: Now Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, “In the past you sought David as your king.

original.text: וּדְבַר אַבְנֵ֣ר הָיָ֔ה עִם זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר גַּם תְּמוֹל֙ גַּם שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם הֱיִיתֶ֞ם מְבַקְשִׁ֧ים אֶת דָּוִ֛ד לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עֲלֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: Now act, because YHWH has spoken concerning David, saying, By hand of David my servant I will save my people Israel from hand of Philistines and from hand of all their enemies.

familiar.text: Now then do it: for the LORD hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.

modern.text: Now take action, because the LORD has said to David, ‘Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה עֲשׂ֑וּ כִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אָמַ֤ר אֶל דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּיַ֣ד דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֗י הוֹשִׁ֜יעַ אֶת עַמִּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִיַּ֣ד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמִיַּ֖ד כָּל אֹיְבֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Abner also spoke in ears of Benjamin. Abner also went to speak in ears of David at Hebron all that was good in eyes of Israel and in eyes of whole house of Benjamin.

familiar.text: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.

modern.text: Abner also spoke to the Benjamites and went to Hebron to tell David all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר גַּם אַבְנֵ֖ר בְּאָזְנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ין וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גַּם אַבְנֵ֗ר לְדַבֵּ֞ר בְּאָזְנֵ֤י דָוִד֙ בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן אֵ֤ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר טוֹב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל בֵּ֥ית בִּנְיָמִֽן

verses.restored: Abner came to David at Hebron, and with him twenty men. David made a feast for Abner and for men who were with him.

familiar.text: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that were with him a feast.

modern.text: When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א אַבְנֵ֤ר אֶל דָּוִד֙ חֶבְר֔וֹן וְאִתּ֖וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּ֨עַשׂ דָּוִ֧ד לְאַבְנֵ֛ר וְלַאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁתֶּֽה

verses.restored: Abner said to David, I will arise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, and they will cut covenant with you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires. David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

familiar.text: And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a league with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thine heart desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.

modern.text: Then Abner said to David, “Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.” So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace. Joab Murders Abner

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְנֵ֣ר אֶל דָּוִ֡ד אָק֣וּמָה וְֽאֵלֵ֡כָה וְאֶקְבְּצָה֩ אֶל אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְיִכְרְת֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּרִ֔ית וּמָ֣לַכְתָּ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר תְּאַוֶּ֖ה נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיְּשַׁלַּ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת אַבְנֵ֖ר וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Look, servants of David and Joab came from a raid and brought much spoil with them. Abner was not with David in Hebron, because David had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.

familiar.text: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from pursuing a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.

modern.text: Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron because David had sent him on his way in peace.

original.text: וְהִנֵּה֩ עַבְדֵ֨י דָוִ֤ד וְיוֹאָב֙ בָּ֣א מֵֽהַגְּד֔וּד וְשָׁלָ֥ל רָ֖ב עִמָּ֣ם הֵבִ֑יאוּ וְאַבְנֵ֗ר אֵינֶ֤נּוּ עִם דָּוִד֙ בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י שִׁלְּח֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Joab and all army that was with him came, and they told Joab, saying, Abner son of Ner came to king, and he sent him away, and he went in peace.

familiar.text: When Joab and all the host that was with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.

modern.text: When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was informed, “Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.”

original.text: וְיוֹאָ֛ב וְכָל הַצָּבָ֥א אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֖וֹ בָּ֑אוּ וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְיוֹאָב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּֽא אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן נֵר֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֖הוּ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Joab came to king and said, What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why is this: you sent him away, and he has gone?

familiar.text: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?

translation_notes: The chapter presents dynastic reproduction through six sons and six named mothers. Women and children must not be reduced to succession inventory.
Rizpah is the subject of a political accusation between men, yet the text gives her no speech or consent. Concubine status does not make sexual access a legitimate token of sovereignty.
Abner changes allegiance after his authority is challenged. His theological language and promise to deliver Israel may combine conviction, anger, survival, and ambition.
David conditions alliance on the return of Michal, invoking a bride-price of mutilated enemy bodies. Neither prior marriage nor royal claim establishes her present consent.

Michal is taken from Paltiel, who follows weeping until Abner orders him away. The scene exposes state power tearing an intimate household apart; it should not be romanticized as rightful restoration.
Joab lures Abner into private conversation and kills him without trial. Blood revenge and security claims do not create due process.

David's curse weaponizes genital discharge, skin disease, mobility dependence, violent death, and hunger as hereditary shame. It must not support ableism, disease stigma, or collective punishment of descendants.

David publicly disavows the killing and genuinely mourns, while also benefiting politically from Abner's death. Public grief does not settle questions of command responsibility or political advantage.
David calls himself weak despite being anointed. Anointing without capacity to restrain one's commanders is not accountable governance.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Center Rizpah and Michal as persons rather than sovereignty markers. Do not justify forced marital transfer, blood revenge, private execution, hereditary curses, disease stigma, or leader claims of helplessness. David's mourning matters, but it does not replace investigation and restraint of Joab.
